title: A Stray Cat Became Station Master And Saved A Railway
description: A stray calico named Tama was made station master of a dying country station in Japan, and passengers started coming back. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tama_(cat) Would you ride a train just to meet a cat? #anime #shorts #animestory #retroanime #truestory #history

characters.Tama: small female calico cat, white fur with orange and black patches, round amber eyes, plain red collar with a small plain gold tag, no clothes; in station master scenes she wears a tiny navy blue conductor cap with a gold band and no badge lettering
characters.Toshiko Koyama: Japanese woman in her 50s in 2006, short permed black hair with some gray, kind round face, beige cardigan over a pale green blouse, dark gray slacks, plain white apron, no hat, no glasses
characters.Mitsunobu Kojima: Japanese businessman in his 60s in 2006, neat short gray hair combed back, thin rimless glasses, dark navy suit, white shirt, plain dark red tie, black leather shoes, no hat

scenes.say: A stray cat saved a dying railway line in Japan. In 2006, tiny Kishi Station in Wakayama lost its last staff, and the cats living there lost their shelter.
scenes.video: [0-4s] At tiny rural Kishi Station in Wakayama in 2006, an empty single wooden platform beside one rail track, green hills behind, quiet late afternoon light. [4-7s] Beside the small wooden Kishi Station building, Tama the calico cat sits alone next to a flattened cardboard box, looking up. [7-10s] On the empty platform of Kishi Station, close-up of Tama's amber eyes as a two-car local train pulls away in the background.

scenes.say: Toshiko Koyama, who regularly fed those strays, begged the railway's new president, Mitsunobu Kojima, to let them live inside the station. One calico caught his eye.
scenes.video: [0-4s] On the wooden platform of Kishi Station, Toshiko Koyama kneels and sets down a small plain dish while Tama eats from it. [4-7s] Inside the small waiting room of Kishi Station, Toshiko Koyama bows deeply to Mitsunobu Kojima, her hands pressed together. [7-10s] Inside the small waiting room of Kishi Station, Mitsunobu Kojima crouches and looks at Tama sitting on a wooden bench, a slow smile forming.

scenes.say: Kojima thought Tama looked like a maneki-neko, the beckoning cat. So on January 5, 2007, he made her station master. Her salary was a year's supply of cat food.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Inside the small waiting room of Kishi Station, close-up of Tama raising one front paw to wash her face, like a beckoning cat. [4-7s] On the platform of Kishi Station on a cold clear winter morning, Mitsunobu Kojima gently places the tiny navy conductor cap on Tama's head while Toshiko Koyama watches, smiling. [7-10s] On a wooden counter inside Kishi Station, Toshiko Koyama sets down one large plain paper sack of cat food beside Tama.

scenes.say: She was good at it. People came just to watch her greet the trains, and that first month, ridership jumped seventeen percent compared to the year before.
scenes.video: [0-4s] On the platform of Kishi Station, Tama in her tiny conductor cap sits upright at the edge of the platform as a two-car train slows to a stop. [4-7s] On the platform of Kishi Station, a young mother and her small son crouch and smile at Tama, the boy reaching out one finger. [7-10s] On the platform of Kishi Station, an elderly man in a brown jacket bows politely to Tama, who blinks slowly back at him.

scenes.say: So the railway kept promoting her. Super station master in 2008, operating officer in 2010. One study said she brought about 1.1 billion yen into the local economy.
scenes.video: [0-4s] Inside a converted ticket booth at Kishi Station, Tama naps on a folded cushion behind the small window, her cap beside her. [4-7s] In front of the new Kishi Station building, a small wooden station shaped like a cat's face with two dormer windows as eyes, Mitsunobu Kojima looks up at it proudly in summer sunlight. [7-10s] Inside the converted ticket booth at Kishi Station, close-up of Tama yawning while Toshiko Koyama laughs softly beside her.

scenes.say: Tama died in 2015 at sixteen. Thousands came to say goodbye, and she was enshrined as a goddess beside her station. Not bad for a stray who once had nowhere to live.
scenes.video: [0-4s] On the platform of Kishi Station on a gray rainy June day, Toshiko Koyama stands quietly holding Tama's tiny navy cap in both hands. [4-7s] At a small wooden Shinto shrine beside Kishi Station, Mitsunobu Kojima bows his head before a small bronze cat statue, rain dripping from the roof. [7-10s] At the same small shrine beside Kishi Station, the rain stops and warm light falls on the bronze cat statue as a two-car train passes softly behind.
